correctness.rationale: Fano incidence gives BBᵀ=BᵀB=2I+J. The eigenvalues ±3 are simple with nonzero coordinates everywhere; each ±√2 eigenspace is parameterized by (x,±Bᵀx/√2), x perpendicular to 1. Vanishing on the detectors is exactly orthogonality to the columns of M(S). For H=A−iD with D nonnegative, an eigenvector with real eigenvalue obeys ⟨ψ,Dψ⟩=0 and is consequently an adjacency eigenvector killed by D. The dark sum of these adjacency subspaces reduces both A and D; on its complement all eigenvalues of −iH have strictly negative real part, so even with Jordan blocks that complement decays. This proves the loss-independent rank and capture fraction, not just a sampled-rate statement. Fewer than six coordinate constraints cannot kill a six-dimensional eigenspace; six point detectors suffice. Each nonzero zero-sum x and y=Bᵀx has support at least two. A two-point difference produces exactly four line coordinates; dually, a two-line difference produces exactly four point coordinates via x=By/2. The source's three-point line-count wording only gives 'at least three'; to exclude equality (3,3), there are in fact six nonzero line sums: for collinear support these are singleton lines; for noncollinear support there are three singleton and three pair lines, with every pair sum the negative of the remaining nonzero entry. Thus equality in the support bound occurs only for the two dipole types, with 21 distinct complements of each type, and any nine detectors suffice. The independent rational enumeration gives rank counts 21/1092/1890 for six, 336/3096 for seven, 42/2961 for eight and 2002 full-rank placements for nine, and directly recovers the eight-set dipoles. For each of the 21 rank-five flags, reducing modulo the three selected point columns leaves the constant column and the two disjoint two-point indicators partitioning the four remaining points; these have rank two, and the selected point-line itself restricts to zero. The exhaustive rank-five total therefore excludes other flags or forms.
residual_risks: Only finite-dimensional coherent adjacency dynamics with fixed strictly positive detector losses and eventual norm capture; no finite-time or absorption-speed conclusion.

evidence: The prior Heawood support bound implies that every five-site complement is safe and at least one six-site complement is unsafe, hence nine is sharp for all placements. The six-detector existence bound also follows readily from spectral multiplicities and choosing point coordinates.

A six-detector complement has eight sites; whether a dark direction survives depends on full incidence-column dependence, not just whether the graph admits some six-site-supported eigenfunction. The catalogue inspects ranks 5, 6 and 7 and distinguishes the labelled placements.

The exact six-set classification supplies additional information not a parameter specialization of the inspected results. evidence: Minimum support six for the Heawood nonprincipal eigenspaces is explicit in the survey; sign-flipping one bipartition transfers either ±√2 eigenspace to the other without changing supports.

Detector success is equivalently that coordinate evaluations span the dual of each nonprincipal eigenspace (a spectral observability/rank test). Its point-line dual has the same ranks. Heawood identifying-code statements concern distinguishing neighborhood signatures rather than this restricted eigenspace rank.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Taking complements translates eigenfunction minimum support precisely into the universal threshold; zero-forcing and identifying-code parameters are not equivalent to the fixed-adjacency spectral condition. A minimum-support number is not an enumeration of all deficient evaluation subsets.

originality.rationale: The distinct supported contribution is the labelled Heawood detector rank census, especially the six-detector breakdown and exact arrangements, rather than the dark-space criterion, Fano spectrum, or placement-independent threshold alone. The placement-independent threshold is already a direct consequence of the established Heawood minimum eigenfunction support six: under positive site losses a placement is bad exactly when its complement contains an eigenfunction support. The known six-support result does not supply the exact catalogue of full-rank six-sets, whose complements leave room for more than minimal supports.
residual_risks: Sotnikova 2018 full text was not recovered; precise priority for the 42 dipole complements is unresolved. The distinctness assessment rests on the exact six-site rank census and geometry, not on absence of a general support theorem.
The bounded search is not comprehensive historical-priority certification.

value.rationale: The Heawood graph is a canonical small incidence network with large eigenspace degeneracies. At the minimum viable detector budget, the exact 1890/3003 success fraction and the distribution of remaining dark dimensions quantify placement sensitivity, something an existential threshold or a minimum support cannot do. The rank-five Fano flags give a geometric explanation of the worst placements at that budget. This motivates the finite exact count independently of the already implied universal threshold.
residual_risks: Graph-specific and asymptotic in time; no general enumeration across projective planes or bound on practical capture time.
